title: Post-quantum Cryptography in the Wild: Assessing the Readiness of Open-Source Ecosystems
abstract: The threat of cryptographically relevant quantum computers, compounded by harvest now, decrypt later attacks, has made migration to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) urgent. With PQC standards finalized and transition guidance phasing out quantum-vulnerable algorithms, the readiness of the open-source supply chain, through which cryptographic vulnerabilities propagate, remains unclear. To fill this gap, we present the first cross-ecosystem empirical study of source-level PQC readiness. PQC Scanner is a two-stage pipeline in which (i) crypto detection identifies packages with cryptographic functionality, and (ii) PQC detection produces a binary support label and source-derived structured readiness record at the repository level using commit history, source analysis, and agent post-verification. Applied to 1,117,913 packages, Stage 1 identifies 55,654 crypto-related packages. Stage 2 evaluates their repositories for source-level PQC support. A separate audit of 219 Stage 2-negative repositories gives a Stage 2 recall lower bound of ≥ 97.48%. On a 247-repository deployment-validation sample, agent post-verification eliminated all false positives, yielding precision of 1.000. The pipeline scales to million-package scans: at concurrency 10, it analyzes over one million packages in just over two weeks, with a median LLM cost of $0.0010 per package. Across 8 ecosystems, we find a migration gap: only 1.88% of crypto-related packages show source-level PQC support, and the repository-deduplicated rate is 1.72%. Rust leads by both counts, while NuGet/Ruby/PHP remain near zero. Source-derived structured readiness records show partial support: among PQC-supporting repositories, only 19.2% satisfy the full-support criterion, with a mean migration coverage of 36%. Adoption accelerates sharply after FIPS publication (August 2024), but migration remains infrastructure-gated: key libraries such as Python’s cryptography (581M downloads/month) and framework integration layers in Java/npm still lack deployable PQC pathways, blocking downstream packages regardless of developer intent. We characterize adoption timing, bottlenecks, and community response strategies, deriving recommendations for maintainers, registry operators, and policy makers.

title: DisMed-LLM: De-Identifying Spanish Medical Text with Large Language Models
abstract: Abstract Patient privacy and compliance with regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) necessitate the robust de-identification of clinical texts. This study investigates the feasibility, computational cost, and limitations of de-identifying Spanish medical records using training-free Large Language Models (LLMs) compared to a supervised baseline. We evaluated five instruction-tuned LLMs on two Spanish clinical corpora (DisMed and MEDDOCAN) and benchmarked them against a fine-tuned multilingual BERT (110M parameters). On a held-out test set, the supervised baseline achieved a strict F1 of 0.904, outperforming the best training-free LLM (Gemma-2 9B, 0.796) while operating roughly 800 times faster. The LLMs’ performance gap was driven entirely by recall and concentrated in categories defined by corpus-specific conventions (e.g., institutions and locations) rather than universal surface forms (names and dates). Testing a newer model (Qwen3-8B) did not resolve this gap, indicating the limitation stems from annotation guidelines rather than model scale. However, when target-corpus annotations were unavailable, the dynamic reversed: in cross-corpus transfer, the supervised model’s F1 collapsed to 0.490, falling below all prompted LLMs, because it rigidly applied the source corpus’s conventions. Finally, novel disclosure metrics revealed that while LLM boundary errors are marginal (0.67%), they miss 26.7% of protected mentions entirely. We conclude that training-free LLMs are a highly adaptable, viable first-pass instrument for institutions lacking annotated data, but their residual disclosure rates mandate human review prior to data release.

title: Barron Optimal Transport I: Generative Modeling
abstract: Motivated by recent applications in generative modeling and sampling, we introduce a framework for optimal measure transport where cost captures the notion of neural network complexity. In transport-based generative models, samples from a reference distribution (e.g. Gaussian) are mapped to samples of a target distribution along ordinary or stochastic differential equations. These are implemented as deep residual networks when discretized in time, where each hidden layer approximates the associated instantaneous velocity. Thus, given a pair of target and reference measures, a natural question is to search for the most efficient neural representation that implements this transport. Our starting point is the kinetic formulation of OT, due to Benamou and Brenier. We replace the average kinetic $L^2$ energy by the \emph{Barron} energy \cite{bach2017breaking, ma2022barron}, a natural norm which measures the complexity of representing a given vector field with a neural hidden layer, and which captures the adaptive properties of feature learning. This defines a metric on the space of probability measures, complementing existing Wasserstein and Stein geometries. In this work we examine the properties of this metric in the context of generative modeling. As a first application, we quantify the suboptimality of diffusion generative modeling in the Barron geometry by establishing super-polynomial score approximation lower bounds for data generated by neural network pushforwards of the Gaussian. We then investigate the benefit of adaptivity as a way to study alternative generative models. In a companion paper \cite{companionpaper} we leverage the Barron transport geometry for sampling applications, extending the scope of Stein variational gradient methods via feature adaptation.

title: SAVU-BENCH: A Real-World Benchmark for Spatial Audio-Visual Understanding
abstract: Spatial audio-visual understanding requires models to recognize not only what is present, but also where events occur and how they relate across modalities. Existing benchmarks often rely on simulated scenes, evaluate isolated spatial skills, and provide limited diagnostic insight into failure modes. We introduce SAVU-Bench, a real-world benchmark that systematically evaluates spatial audio-visual understanding across three capability levels and seven evaluation tasks. We further introduce SAVU-Diag, a scene-linked diagnostic set that decomposes reasoning questions into their prerequisite grounding and alignment sub-tasks. Evaluation of 12 representative models on SAVU-Bench reveals that while visual spatial grounding is relatively mature, spatial perception involving audio remains a primary bottleneck. SAVU-Diag further demonstrates that most reasoning errors co-occur with failures on these prerequisite tasks, though reasoning gaps persist even when prerequisites are correctly resolved. Motivated by these findings, we introduce SAVU-EA, a training-free evidence-augmented baseline that makes spatial cues more explicit. While SAVU-EA substantially improves spatial grounding and joint matching, high-level spatial reasoning remains challenging. Our findings highlight the urgent need for both robust spatial audio perception and deeper integration of cross-modal spatial relations.

title: Asymptotic Stability of Domain Walls for One Dimensional Schrödinger Map with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
abstract: In this paper, we study the long time dynamics of small perturbations of static domain walls in weighted Sobolev spaces for the one dimensional Schrödinger map with constant Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. The perturbation equation contains derivative nonlinearities, and its linearized operator has a threshold resonance. The results are twofold. (i) We prove the asymptotic stability of the domain wall modulo the translation and rotation symmetries. More precisely, the corresponding modulation parameters converge as time tends to infinity, while the radiation decays at the sharp rate t^{-1/2}. (ii) We prove that the radiation exhibits modified scattering, with an explicit logarithmic phase correction generated by the long range cubic interaction. The proof develops geometric reduction to overcome the loss of derivatives and exploits structural cancellations in the nonlinear interactions.

title: Excitation Spectra of the Frustrated Spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Model via Dual Spin-Sector Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
abstract: Finding excited states and excitation gaps in frustrated spin systems using Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQE) is complicated by state-ordering inversions. In the frustrated spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model, standard single-sector algorithms like Variational Quantum Deflation (VQD) in $S_z=0$ fail when $J_2/J_1 < 0.25$. In this regime, the lowest-lying excitation in $S_z=0$ is a Triplet ($S=1$), which lies below the Excited Singlet ($S=0$). Standard deflation projects out the ground singlet and converges onto the Triplet state, misidentifying it as the Excited Singlet. Here, this work presents a Dual Spin-Sector VQE framework that resolves these state-ordering inversions applied to frustrated $J_1-J_2$ models on 1D spin chains and 2D rectangular lattices. Firstly, by optimizing the ground Triplet state in the $S_z=1$ sector (where singlet states cannot exist), mapping it into $S_z=0$ via the total spin-lowering operator $S^- = \sum_i S_i^-$, and evaluating a dual-sector penalty cost function, the Excited Singlet ($E_S$) is isolated without variational ambiguity. Numerical state-vector simulations confirm exact convergence to machine precision with unit overlap fidelity. The method captures key physical features, including the gapless phase, the gapless-gapped critical point at $J_2/J_1 \approx 0.2411$, the Majumdar-Ghosh dimer point ($J_2/J_1 = 0.50$), and the 2D non-magnetic frustrated regime ($J_2/J_1 \approx 0.40 - 0.60$). Finite-shot sampling simulations and gate-scaling analytics up to $N=100$ qubits demonstrate the resource efficiency and shot resilience of the algorithm for near-term quantum execution.

evidence.title: Excitation Spectra of the Frustrated Spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Model via Dual Spin-Sector Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
evidence.abstract: Finding excited states and excitation gaps in frustrated spin systems using Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQE) is complicated by state-ordering inversions. In the frustrated spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model, standard single-sector algorithms like Variational Quantum Deflation (VQD) in $S_z=0$ fail when $J_2/J_1 < 0.25$. In this regime, the lowest-lying excitation in $S_z=0$ is a Triplet ($S=1$), which lies below the Excited Singlet ($S=0$). Standard deflation projects out the ground singlet and converges onto the Triplet state, misidentifying it as the Excited Singlet. Here, this work presents a Dual Spin-Sector VQE framework that resolves these state-ordering inversions applied to frustrated $J_1-J_2$ models on 1D spin chains and 2D rectangular lattices. Firstly, by optimizing the ground Triplet state in the $S_z=1$ sector (where singlet states cannot exist), mapping it into $S_z=0$ via the total spin-lowering operator $S^- = \sum_i S_i^-$, and evaluating a dual-sector penalty cost function, the Excited Singlet ($E_S$) is isolated without variational ambiguity. Numerical state-vector simulations confirm exact convergence to machine precision with unit overlap fidelity. The method captures key physical features, including the gapless phase, the gapless-gapped critical point at $J_2/J_1 \approx 0.2411$, the Majumdar-Ghosh dimer point ($J_2/J_1 = 0.50$), and the 2D non-magnetic frustrated regime ($J_2/J_1 \approx 0.40 - 0.60$). Finite-shot sampling simulations and gate-scaling analytics up to $N=100$ qubits demonstrate the resource efficiency and shot resilience of the algorithm for near-term quantum execution.

title: OrthoGen: A Generative Orthogonal Learner for Time-Varying Treatments
abstract: Estimating conditional distributional potential outcomes (CDPOs) over time is important in medicine (e.g., to estimate patient-specific risks under different treatment sequences). However, this task is challenging because of time-varying confounding, yet existing adjustment strategies for this task are limited. In this paper, we aim to learn CDPOs under time-varying treatments using flexible generative models. Our contributions are two-fold. (1) We introduce a tailored adjustment strategy for our setting, namely, generative recursive g-computation. Our adjustment strategy recursively propagates full conditional outcome distributions rather than conditional means, modeling the variables of interest directly rather than full trajectories. Building on our adjustment strategy, we formulate simple generative learners for CDPO estimation. However, these learners can be sensitive to nuisance estimation errors, which motivates an orthogonal learner. (2) We thus introduce OrthoGen, a Neyman-orthogonal and doubly robust generative learner. Importantly, we show that OrthoGen further achieves rate double robustness and quasi-oracle efficiency under suitable conditions. Our learners are flexible and can be instantiated with different generative backbones (e.g., normalizing flows and diffusion models). Across experiments with synthetic, semi-synthetic and real-world datasets, we find that OrthoGen is highly effective. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to propose a generative orthogonal learner for estimating CDPOs under time-varying treatments.

title: Fast holographic inversion of superconducting domes
abstract: A holographic superconductor whose scalar mass depends on the gauge field strength, $M(\Fsq)$, reproduces a superconducting dome for a suitable $M$, and recovering that $M$ from a given dome has so far taken days for a single training run. We propose a new way of training this model, with which an inversion takes from about ten minutes to an hour. Training needs the gradient of the condition that fixes the critical temperature, which the earlier method obtains by finite differences, repeating the bulk integrations for every training parameter. Here that condition is obtained, without any fit, from two integrations started at the horizon and at the boundary, and its derivative with respect to $M$ is an integral over the same two solutions, so the gradient needs no integration of its own. We use the speed to study the part of $M$ that a dome cannot determine, on the interval between the value $\Fsq$ takes at the horizon for the lowest doping and $\Fsq=0$, at which $M$ is the scalar mass $M(0)$ that fixes the dimension of the dual operator. We hold the scalar mass at several values, which we call pinned masses, retrain everything else at each, and find that the reconstructions agree wherever the horizons of the dome reach, including the minima of $M$, and differ only on that interval. A rule that keeps the reconstruction with the simplest closed form recovers both the scalar mass and the mass function of a test dome. On Gaussian and double-Gaussian domes and on the measured phase diagrams of YBa$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{y}$ and 2M-WS$_{2}$, however, the pinned mass it keeps rests on ties or on narrow margins, so for these targets the scalar mass is left open. The dome thus constrains $M$ where its horizons reach, and fixing the dimension of the dual operator needs a second observable.

title: EM-SNN: Efficiently Modulated Spiking Neural Network for Remote Sensing Image Dehazing
abstract: Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) provide an energy-efficient alternative to artificial neural networks (ANNs), their application to remote sensing image dehazing remains limited. A key challenge arises from the coupling between haze-induced high-frequency attenuation and discrete spike thresholding. This interaction suppresses weak responses and fundamentally limits the recovery of edges, textures, and fine details in spiking dehazing models. To address this challenge, we propose the Efficiently Modulated Spiking Neural Network (EM-SNN), a dedicated spiking framework tailored to remote sensing image dehazing. EM-SNN integrates a statistics-driven Threshold-Modulated Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (TM-LIF) neuron to adaptively compensate for haze-induced contrast compression, together with a Spike Sobel Modulation (SSM) module that enhances structural cues and reduces depth-wise attenuation during spiking feature propagation. By jointly modulating activation scales and structural representations, EM-SNN improves dehazing performance while preserving the inherent event-driven sparsity of SNNs. Experiments on HRSD, RICE, RRSHID, and SateHaze1K demonstrate that EM-SNN achieves competitive dehazing performance while consuming only one quarter of the energy of the strong ANN baseline SFRDP-Net.

title: Sistem Pakar Deteksi Dini Komplikasi Kehamilan Menggunakan Metode Certainty Factor
abstract: Pregnancy is an important phase that requires careful monitoring due to the risk of complications that may endanger the health of the mother and fetus. At Doa Ibu Persada Clinic, Langkat Regency, the identification of pregnancy complications is still conducted through anamnesis and direct medical examinations by healthcare personnel. The main problem is the absence of a screening system that can assist in identifying possible complications based on symptoms experienced by pregnant women. This study aims to develop a web-based expert system for the early detection of pregnancy complications using the Certainty Factor method. The system uses five types of complications, namely preeclampsia, anemia, gestational diabetes, pregnancy bleeding, and pregnancy infection, supported by 23 symptoms as the knowledge base. The Certainty Factor method combines expert confidence values with user confidence levels for selected symptoms to determine the confidence level of each diagnosis. The implementation using a patient case showed that preeclampsia obtained the highest Certainty Factor value of 0.9939 or 99.39%, making it the primary diagnosis. This result is consistent with the manual calculation conducted in the study. Therefore, the developed expert system can assist the early identification of pregnancy complications and provide diagnostic confidence information as preliminary support before further medical examination.

title: Finite-Time Sampling of Dynamic Spectral Information: Early Blindness, Local Identifiability, and Global Collisions
abstract: We investigate whether a finite set of temporal slices of a dynamic spectral feature canpreserve the distinguishing power of the full trajectory. The basis is a two-qubit family ofgeneratorsK(J, h) = JX1X2 + h(Z1 + Z2), J > 0, r = h/J > 0,for which a precise three-branch formula for the maximized commutator magnitude waspreviously obtained in [1]:D(x, r) = max{F0(x), F1(x, r), Fmix(x, r)}.For two subsystems, the spectrum of the weighted Laplacian is fully equivalent to D(x, r),which reduces the identification problem to the analysis of a single scalar function.The paper distinguishes three levels of temporal design properties: early blindness, localidentifiability, and global distinguishability. We prove analytically the existence of earlyblindness with respect to the field parameter and of universal blind lines. We numericallyfind and certify regular collisions for a six-slice design: two distinct models coincide on allslices but differ along the full trajectory.The main result is a rigorous example of a finite-time design in a fully controllable twoqubit quantum model that is locally informative but globally does not distinguish two distinctmodels. We find 20 distinct collisions for the six-slice design; one of them is certified viathe Krawczyk method (existence and uniqueness of the root). The exact minimal number ofdistinguishing temporal slices remains open.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Driven Enterprise Knowledge Base
abstract: As enterprises generate vast amounts of heterogeneous knowledge, existing knowledge management systems face challenges in providing contextually relevant, accurate, and domain-specific answers. To address these issues, the authors propose KQGen, a unified framework that integrates knowledge graph embeddings with generative question answering for enterprise knowledge bases. KQGen encodes knowledge graph entities and relations, performs query understanding, and generates answers grounded in structured knowledge, optimized by a reinforcement learning-based feedback mechanism. Experimental results on benchmarks such as SQuAD, TREC, and KBQA show that KQGen outperforms existing models in answer relevance and ranking metrics. However, challenges remain in improving performance for Exact Match (EM) and scalability. Future work will focus on refining multi-hop reasoning, real-time scalability, and integrating multi-modal data for enhanced system adaptability.

title: Investigating mental wellbeing in the construction industry using social media sentiment analysis: a UK case study
abstract: Mental health challenges represent a significant global concern, with depression affecting approximately 4% of the population. In the United Kingdom, approximately one in four individuals will experience a mental health problem, with the construction industry particularly vulnerable due to its demanding work environment. This investigation employs a historical dataset (May 2008 to March 2016) to establish the methodological feasibility of social media sentiment analysis for detecting occupational stress indicators in construction-related discourse. Rather than claiming contemporary generalizability, this work demonstrates proof-of-concept that automated sentiment analysis can reliably detect emotional patterns from social media data. By leveraging user-generated content from Twitter, 2,322 tweets were extracted and subjected to exploratory analysis, sentiment analysis, topic modelling analysis, and machine learning classification. Emotion labels were assigned using NRCLex lexicon-based methods and validated against human ratings (κ = 0.79). Machine learning classifiers were applied to categorise tweets into different emotions using n-grams as input features. Results indicated that uni-gram features offered superior performance across all classifiers compared to bi-gram and tri-gram feature sets. When trained with default hyperparameters, traditional machine learning methods such as logistic regression and support vector classifier achieved comparable performance to neural network methods in detecting anticipation emotion (AUC 0.93 vs 0.90), with similar patterns observed for other emotion categories. Topic modelling identified ten substantive themes in construction-related discourse, with employment security concerns embedded throughout technical discussions. The findings establish methodological proof-of-concept for real-time sentiment monitoring in occupational settings, with recommendations for contemporary replication to assess current construction industry emotional patterns.

title: A Controlled Benchmark of Deep Segmentation Architectures for Mammographic Microcalcification Segmentation on CBIS-DDSM: Evidence Consistent with an Annotation-Related Performance Limit
abstract: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer in women worldwide, and clustered microcalcifications on mammography are among its earliest indicators. Automated segmentation of microcalcifications is challenging because the calcifications are small, sparse, and often embedded in dense fibroglandular tissue. In addition, publicly available datasets such as CBIS-DDSM provide annotations at the calcification-cluster level rather than for individual calcification particles. Although numerous deep-learning architectures have been proposed for this task, their relative performance under a common experimental framework remains unclear. This study presents a rigorous, leakage-controlled benchmark of ten segmentation architectures, including convolutional models (U-Net, nnU-Net, BreastNet, ConvNeXt-UNet), an attention-gated model (Attention U-Net), convolution-transformer hybrids (TransUNet, Swin-UNet, MedFormer, UNETR), and MAFT-Net, a multi-scale attention network incorporating dilated convolutions, squeeze-and-excitation gating, self-attention, and gated feature fusion. All models were trained from scratch using identical preprocessing, augmentation, optimisation, and patient-disjoint train/test partitions on the CBIS-DDSM calcification subset. Performance was evaluated using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Intersection-over-Union (IoU), 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and classification AUC. Across all architectures, Dice scores were confined to a narrow range (0.076-0.114), with most pairwise differences failing to reach statistical significance. Increasing architectural complexity, including transformer-based models containing up to 89 million parameters, did not produce consistent performance gains. ROI occupancy analysis showed a strong positive association between Dice and annotation size, with mean Dice increasing from 0.023 to 0.255 across occupancy quartiles. These findings suggest that segmentation performance on CBIS-DDSM is influenced more by the region-level annotation format than by architectural innovation, highlighting an important limitation when interpreting reported overlap metrics.

title: Human or AI-generated synthetic cause agents? Perceived organizational empathy and prosocial engagement in charitable communication
abstract: Purpose This study examines consumer responses to human versus AI-generated synthetic cause agents in charitable communication. It tests whether cause agent type affects three prosocial engagement outcomes with the cause, namely information seeking, willingness to donate and sharing intention, through perceived organizational empathy, and whether this process depends on beneficiary safeguarding framing and beneficiary vulnerability. Design/methodology/approach Three online experiments with US adult Prolific participants and a supplementary Chinese replication were conducted. The replication tested robustness using consequential donation behavior and perceived organizational warmth and perceived organizational morality as competing mechanisms. Study 1 tested the baseline effect of cause agent type and mediation by perceived organizational empathy. Study 2 examined beneficiary safeguarding framing as a moderator. Study 3 introduced beneficiary vulnerability as a higher-order boundary condition. Findings AI-generated synthetic agents reduced perceived organizational empathy and prosocial engagement compared with human cause agents, and perceived organizational empathy mediated these effects. Beneficiary safeguarding framing attenuated this disadvantage. When beneficiary vulnerability was low, human agents were favored under low safeguarding framing, but the difference was no longer significant under high safeguarding framing. When vulnerability was high, no significant differences between human and synthetic agents were observed. Originality/value This research identifies cause agent type as a representational signal in AI-enabled charitable communication and shows how its effect varies with beneficiary safeguarding and vulnerability.

title: CARES: A Controlled Synthetic Benchmark of Speaker Reactions to Sound
abstract: Automatic audio scene description turns a recording into a text account of a situation. One difficulty is deciding which elements of the audio should be kept, since a description cannot include them all. Annotators disagree about this, making a ground truth hard to obtain. In this work, we first define the ground truth, then generate the data. We focus on audio events and define sound salience with a simple rule: a sound is salient when a speaker audibly reacts to it. For scale and variety, a controlled set of scenarios fixes the ground truth, and a language model writes the dialogues. The resulting corpus, CARES, contains 10,000 two-speaker scenes. We then benchmark six audio-language models on three tasks: identifying the scene, tagging the sounds present, and classifying reactions. We show that these models hear the sounds but miss how the speakers react to them.

For scale and variety, a controlled set of scenarios fixes the ground truth, and a language model writes the dialogues. The resulting corpus, CARES, contains 10,000 two-speaker scenes. We then benchmark six audio-language models on three tasks: identifying the scene, tagging the sounds present, and classifying reactions. We show that these models hear the sounds but miss how the speakers react to them.

title: Where Can a Decision Model Diagnose HVAC Faults? Reasoning Demand, Physical Representation, and Robustness Under Shift
abstract: Artificial intelligence supports building operations in several forms, each with its own barrier. Expert rules must be tuned for every system, supervised models need labeled data that buildings rarely record, and language models return free text that requires human-in-the-loop checking, since their stated confidence is unreliable. A newer kind of pretrained model, here called a decision model, returns a probability for every allowed answer, so one model could serve many decisions without training. This study answers three open questions for fault diagnosis in heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems: which decisions such a model can make, what input it needs, and whether its probabilities hold when conditions change. On 128 fault days from four public datasets of real equipment, faults are graded by the reasoning their diagnosis demands, with data given raw, as physical features, or with Brick topology. The decision model Jev, open language models, and a supervised model face nine tests that change season, control configuration, or building. Given physical features, Jev and the larger open model diagnosed faults whose evidence one feature carries, but not faults that need operating context. Under shift they kept their accuracy and calibration, while the supervised model lost 0.33 macro-F1 yet led or tied within a building. Their probabilities still needed correction, and detection was weak. The study maps which faults a decision model can diagnose and from what input, and supports a division of work in which code computes the physics and the model ranks candidate faults for an operator.

title: Optimal (Parallel) Spooky Pebbling on Binary Trees
abstract: Pebble games model computations under a fixed space budget. Spooky pebbling allows quantum memory to be released by measurement, with the resulting phases corrected later. We study two-input computations with binary-tree dependencies and determine the optimal work and parallel depth for complete binary trees. Our key idea is to clean up the tree in blocks, reducing repeated recomputation of intermediate values. For the complete tree $B_h$ with $n=2^h-1$ vertices and every space budget $h+1\le s\le n$, we give an algorithm with asymptotically optimal work $Θ(nh/\log(s+1))$. At the minimum budget $s=h+1$, this improves the $O(n\log n)$ bound of Kornerup, Sadun, and Soloveichik to $Θ(n\log n/\log\log n)$, resolving their time-optimality question. We also construct a parallel schedule with optimal depth \[ Θ\!\left(h+\frac ns \max\!\left\{\frac{h}{\log(s+1)},\,1+\log^*h\right\}\right). \] Our lower bounds hold for every full binary tree. We also show that achieving optimal parallel depth can require asymptotically more work than minimizing work alone. Applying our schedule to the RNS point-addition trees in the public implementation of Chevignard, Fouque, and Schrottenloher reduces their Toffoli/AND gate count by $20.86\%$ for a P-224 instance and $22.66\%$ for a P-256 instance, using the same arithmetic circuits and peak workspace.

title: Hardware-aware Calibrated Clustered Attention for Efficient Visual Geometric Transformers
abstract: The Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) marks a significant leap forward in 3D scene reconstruction, as it is the first model that directly infers all key 3D attributes (camera poses, depths, and dense geometry) jointly in one pass. However, this joint inference mechanism requires global attention layers with extremely long sequences that causes a significant latency bottleneck. In this paper, we propose blockwise clustered attention (BC attention) to accelerate the global attention layers in VGGT. By limiting the clustering within HW-friendly neighborhood blocks, BC attention reduces the computation overhead of query clustering as well as the costly data movement between on- and off-chip memory. This enables BC attention to scale to long sequences and deliver practical latency improvements on GPUs. Moreover, we introduce a hashing hyperplane calibration method and a threshold-based error compensation method to reduce clustering errors efficiently, which is a bottleneck in the current clustered attention mechanism. Overall, our experiments on GPU demonstrate that calibrated BC attention accelerates the global attention layers by 2.10-2.63$\times$ and the whole backbone by 1.77-2.35$\times$ with negligible loss (1%) for large scenes. With a small performance loss (< 5%), calibrated BC attention further achieves a 2.26-2.87$\times$ latency improvement on the global attention layers and a 1.90-2.55$\times$ improvement on the backbone.

title: Explainable NLP in the Era of Large Language Models: A Unified Taxonomy, Evaluation Frameworks, and Decision Guidance
abstract: Explanation methods for natural language processing (NLP) come from two literatures that rarely meet: feature attribution and probing for task models, and the interpretability of large language models (LLMs), from chain-of-thought reasoning to sparse autoencoder features and circuit tracing. We place both in a unified taxonomy with four dimensions: scope (local vs. global), mechanism (how the explanation is computed), model access (model-agnostic vs. model-specific), and output form (importance scores, rules, examples, counterfactuals, rationale spans, concepts, natural language). Faithfulness and plausibility come apart, and the erasure tests built for extracted rationales do not apply to a chain of thought, which is an output rather than part of the input, so chains of thought need intervention tests of their own. The access a deployment allows settles which mechanisms are usable before scope or audience matter; our practical decision frameworks start from that question and are traced through three worked deployments. In our synthesis of LLM-era interpretability, a lineage table shows that most current techniques rebuild or extend older ideas under new constraints of scale and access, while two problems are new: keeping reasoning traces monitorable under training pressure, and testing whether models can introspect. Faithfulness metrics disagree with one another, and sparse autoencoders do not yet beat simple baselines on standardized benchmarks, so evaluations should name the tests they ran instead of reporting one score. We also survey applications across healthcare, legal and financial services, social science research, content moderation, and education, and close with six open problems.

title: Het gebruik van qudits voor fouttolerante kwantum computatie
abstract: Qudits can be described by a state vector in a q-dimensional Hilbert space, enabling a more extensive encoding and manipulation of information compared to qubits. This implies that conducting fault-tolerant quantum computations using qudits rather than qubits might entail less overhead. In this work, I investigate the viability of qudits across three key components of a fault-tolerant quantum computer: hardware control, quantum error-correction codes, and logical gate operations. This includes benchmarking physically decomposed qudit gates against qubit-based implementations for a specific donor-spin system, threshold simulations of qudit error-correction codes using tailored simulators and decoders, and simulations of magic state distillation circuits with qudits. At the hardware level, a numerical leakage-aware randomized benchmarking protocol is applied to a native ququart encoding in a donor-spin system and compared against an equivalent pair of encoded qubits. The ququart implementation is found to reduce the lower-bound gate infidelity by 40 – 50%, a consequence of the fewer ESR and EDSR pulses and correspondingly lower cumulative noise exposure. This provides a concrete, platform-specific demonstration of reduced physical-gate overhead prior to the introduction of any error-correction redundancy. At the level of quantum error correction, the viability of qudits is investigated through the construction and simulation of the quantum circuits for the five-qudit perfect code. The code is evaluated under a multidimensional circuit-level noise model using decoders specifically adapted to the qudit setting. This yields the first threshold estimates reported for qutrit and ququint codes under circuit-level noise. After introducing a flag qudit to protect the code from hook errors, comparable error thresholds of the order of 10–4 are obtained for qudits of dimensions 2, 3 and 5. These simulations were subsequently performed using Sdim, a stabilizer tableau simulator that enabled threshold estimation up to dimension q = 7, a regime inaccessible to state-vector simulators such as Cirq. At the level of logical operations, magic state distillation protocols of the Bravyi-Kitaev type are simulated under logical circuit-level noise, to my knowledge for the first time for this protocol family. Once the Clifford operations implementing the distillation circuit are subject to a nonzero logical error rate, the achievable output fidelity saturates within a finite usable distillation range rather than an arbitrarily improvable one: roughly 0.9-15.6% for the |T⟩₂-type protocol, 3.7-5% for the |H⟩₂-type protocol and 5.4-7.4% for the |H+⟩₃-type protocol at a representative logical circuit-level noise level of pCL = 10–3. The qutrit protocol achieves a more favorable distillation threshold but suffers from a substantially lower yield due to its reduced syndrome acceptance probability. This highlights a trade-off between threshold performance and yield that is intrinsic to the higher-dimensional construction. Further investigation with more advanced and larger-scale protocols is required to better understand and characterize this behavior. Overall, these results show that qudits can provide real efficiency benefits: higher-dimensional control can improve physical gate fidelity, and qutrit and ququint error-correction thresholds can match those of qubits when hook errors are properly handled. However, logical circuit-level noise limits the maximum magic state fidelity, showing that the benefits of qudits are not yet fully realized at the logical-operation level. This thesis provides the first broad numerical study of these effects and introduces the simulation tools needed to explore larger code families, decoders, and distillation protocols.

title: CHATBOT MARKETING EFFORTS, COMMUNICATION QUALITY, USAGE MOTIVATION : DAMPAK TERHADAP SATISFACTION, REUSE INTENTION, PURCHASE INTENTION, DAN E-TRUST
abstract: The use of chatbots on e-commerce platforms is increasingly expanding as a means to enhance customer service quality. Consequently, it is crucial to understand the factors influencing user satisfaction and their impact on user behavior regarding chatbot usage. This study aims to analyze the influence of Chatbot Marketing Efforts on Chatbot Communication Quality; the influence of Chatbot Communication Quality and Motivation for Chatbot Usage on Satisfaction; and the influence of Satisfaction on Reuse Intention, Purchase Intention, and E-Trust. A quantitative approach was employed using purposive sampling involving 530 Shopee users who were at least 17 years old, had used the chatbot feature, and possessed shopping experience on Shopee. Data analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The results indicate that all path coefficients show a positive direction and all tested relationships between variables are significant. Chatbot Marketing Efforts positively influence Chatbot Communication Quality; Chatbot Communication Quality and Motivation for Chatbot Usage positively influence Satisfaction; and Satisfaction positively influences Reuse Intention, Purchase Intention, and E-Trust. This study contributes to the development of chatbot service strategies for e-commerce platforms. It is recommended that Shopee optimize its knowledge base, improve chatbot response quality, and periodically evaluate the user experience to enhance user satisfaction.

title: Investigación científica en la era de la inteligencia artificial innovación, tecnología y transformación digital
abstract: La empresa científica moderna se construyó en torno a una certeza elemental: el ser humano, guiado por la duda metódica y el rigor empírico, era el único artífice legítimo de la interrogación a la naturaleza. Esta premisa, sostenida a lo largo de siglos mediante la acumulación paulatina de evidencia y la formulación teórica pausada, atraviesa hoy una transformación sin precedentes. La confluencia entre la computación cuántica incipiente, los modelos predictivos generativos y la automatización de laboratorios no solo ha acelerado los tiempos de procesamiento; ha alterado la propia dinámica con la que formulamos preguntas, diseñamos experimentos y validamos hallazgos. Este volumen toma distancia deliberada de dos posturas que entorpecen la discusión académica: el entusiasmo acrítico ante la novedad algorítmica y la resistencia nostálgica frente al cambio metodológico. Por el contrario, su propósito es examinar con sobriedad las tensiones epistémicas que emergen cuando los sistemas automatizados predicen configuraciones moleculares complejas en días o generan hipótesis operativas sin mediación deductiva directa. El núcleo del debate contemporáneo ya no gira en torno a la potencia del cálculo, sino a la naturaleza misma del saber. Fenómenos recurrentes como la opacidad inherente a los modelos de caja negra, la crisis de replicabilidad asociada a la fuga inadvertida de datos (data leakage) o la generación de fuentes bibliográficas apócrifas evidencian una frontera crítica: la optimización de correlaciones estadísticas no equivale, bajo ninguna circunstancia, a la comprensión causal de un fenómeno. La actividad científica no se reduce a un inventario probabilístico de aciertos; demanda justificación teórica, contrastación contextual y una responsabilidad ética orientada al bienestar colectivo. A lo largo de los capítulos que integran esta obra, el lector hallará un análisis articulado que conjuga el aprovechamiento técnico de estas herramientas con la exigencia deontológica indispensable en la labor investigativa. Lejos de proponer una sustitución instrumental o un mero recetario procedimental, el texto plantea un ejercicio de discernimiento: reconocer la capacidad de cómputo como un recurso de ampliación analítica, reservando el juicio crítico, el compromiso epistémico y el sentido de propósito a la labor insustituible del investigador.

title: Neural Question Generation: A Survey of Techniques, Question Types, and Applications
abstract: Neural Question Generation (NQG) has emerged as a foundation for educational technologies and automated assessments. In this study, we perform a survey of NQG over its emerging era from 2020 to 2026. To assess a pool of 109 highly relevant research articles, we systematically follow a five-phase identification and filtering approach. Using this analysis, the study proposes an exhaustive taxonomy that classifies the recent advancements in NQG based on question generation methodology, generation type, input modality, datasets, application domain, control objectives, and evaluation metrics. The findings indicate that there is a paradigm shift in NQG methodologies from rule-based and syntactic heuristics to highly advanced and popular Transformer-based methodologies, accounting for 58% of the methodologies. The results also indicate that although multiple-choice questions are the most prevalent question type in NQG methodologies, there is an increasing trend towards the generation of cognitively complex questions. Furthermore, we conclude that NQG approaches suffer from a lack of appropriate evaluation measures as well as an inability to generate questions at the higher cognitive order of Bloom’s Taxonomy.

The findings indicate that there is a paradigm shift in NQG methodologies from rule-based and syntactic heuristics to highly advanced and popular Transformer-based methodologies, accounting for 58% of the methodologies. The results also indicate that although multiple-choice questions are the most prevalent question type in NQG methodologies, there is an increasing trend towards the generation of cognitively complex questions. Furthermore, we conclude that NQG approaches suffer from a lack of appropriate evaluation measures as well as an inability to generate questions at the higher cognitive order of Bloom’s Taxonomy.

title: Transformed Samplers with Variance Reduction
abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods are the standard tool for computing expectations under complex probability distributions. Control variates reduce the variance of the resulting estimates, but a good control variate requires solving the Poisson equation of the sampler, which rarely admits a closed-form solution. Exact solutions are available when the sampler's kernel has a known spectral decomposition on a simple reference density. In our work, we extend these solutions to general targets through a learned change of variables. A bijection, such as a normalizing flow, is trained so that the target becomes close to the reference in a latent space, and we show that Markov kernels and their Poisson solutions are transformed by any bijection. Running such samplers in the latent space then yields explicit control variates, and the estimator is consistent under mild tail conditions on the map and target. Importance sampling (IS) from the flow is the limiting case of the same construction and the control variates apply to it as well. Experiments on synthetic targets and real posteriors compare the procedure against state-of-the-art samplers and control variates.

title: Quantum non-Markovian response spectra
abstract: Quantum systems are rarely isolated from their surroundings. These hidden environments can retain information and return it later, producing correlated errors in quantum computers and complicating the interpretation of experiments. On a quantum processor, for example, one job can therefore leave an environmental trace that affects the next, even after the qubits themselves have been reset. Learning how this hidden influence persists and affects later behavior is therefore important, but the environment is often impossible to measure directly, and fully reconstructing its effects through tomography rapidly becomes impractical. Here, we introduce a response matrix that uses controlled interventions and observations of the system alone to reveal the temporal structure of environmental memory. The matrix records how future observations change across different controlled histories. Its spectrum characterizes how memory is structured and how it persists under specified system resets, while suitable linear combinations of its entries can rule out specified classical models of that memory. Because its history-future queries can be evaluated independently, numerical response matrices can be assembled in parallel. We establish the framework theoretically, characterize response spectra in an interacting spin process, and certify quantum memory in a two-qubit benchmark. This approach turns system observations into a probe of inaccessible environments and could support the diagnosis of correlated noise, tests of open system models, and memory-aware control design.

title: Computations of the slice genus and the unknotting number of links via machine learning
abstract: Links are disjoint unions of circles smoothly embedded in $S^3$. We use reinforcement learning and Bayesian optimisation to obtain new upper bounds on several link invariants that are not known to be algorithmically computable: the slice genus and the unknotting number for links, and the strong slice genus for algebraically split links. We also compute lower bounds using known invariants. Combining the upper and lower bounds, we obtain new exact values in many cases. Our unknotting agents can reproduce the non-additivity of the unknotting number for several counterexamples due to Brittenham and Hermiller, in some cases finding new unknotting trajectories.

title: Gaussian Material Fields for Volumetric Multi-Energy CT Decomposition
abstract: Volumetric material decomposition in multi-energy computed tomography requires a representation that organizes multiple three-dimensional material fields in a common spatial domain while retaining differences in composition and local structure. We observe that spatial primitives can be shared across materials without tying their coefficients, but their local capacity must respond to material-specific reconstruction needs. We introduce Gaussian material fields, which represent multiple material distributions with shared anisotropic 3D Gaussian primitives and independent nonnegative material coefficients. The shared geometry defines a continuous spatial basis, while the coefficients determine each primitive's contribution to the individual material fields. To reconstruct this representation from multi-energy projections, a differentiable spectral forward model combines Gaussian material path integrals with a calibrated basis matrix, enabling joint optimization of spatial geometry and material composition. Material-aware adaptive density control retains material-specific refinement evidence before aggregation and adjusts local representation capacity to accommodate both spatially extensive components and sparse details. Experiments use synthesized multi-energy projections generated from pseudo-reference material maps constructed by conventional methods from publicly available CT data. Across 15 cases, our approach improves average PSNR by 4.03 dB and SSIM by 4.96% over the strongest baseline, while reducing NRMSE by 33.45%. Material-wise comparisons and component ablations support improved recovery of localized structures, while runtime and memory measurements show favorable computational scaling. These results establish Gaussian material fields as an explicit, adaptive representation for volumetric multi-material reconstruction.

title: Perturbative Variational Quantum Eigensolver via Reduced Density Matrices
abstract: Abstract Current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain limited in their ability to perform accurate quantum chemistry simulations because of restricted numbers of high-fidelity qubits and short coherence times. To overcome these challenges, we introduce a reduced-density-matrix (RDM)-based perturbative variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) framework that augments active-space VQE with perturbation theory to recover electron correlation beyond the active space without increasing the qubit count or variational circuit depth. We formulated a fully coupled approach (VQE-PTs) and a diagonal approximation (VQE-PT). The former retains couplings among orthonormalized perturbers, whereas the latter neglects these couplings to simplify the classical postprocessing. Numerical simulations of HF, N2, and F2 show that VQE-PTs provides a robust formulation across different molecular systems, while VQE-PT offers an efficient approximation. We further experimentally implement VQE-PT on the Quafu superconducting quantum processor for F2, achieving a mean absolute error of 1.2 mHa along the potential energy surface after error mitigation. These results demonstrate perturbative VQE as a practical framework for incorporating dynamic correlations in quantum chemistry simulations.

title: IA na gestão executiva
abstract: IA na gestão executiva apresenta um percurso de aplicação de inteligência artificial para executivos, diretores, gestores e empreendedores.O objetivo do livro é ajudar o leitor a transformar informação fragmentada em decisões executadas, com impacto visível em margem, produtividade e experiência do cliente. O conteúdo usa casos didáticos fictícios, exemplos e propostas de trabalho para discutir decisões, organização de informações e revisão humana.Ao longo dos 10 capítulos, você encontrará:IA para líderes: capacidades, custos e limitaçõesMapeamento de oportunidades por impacto e esforçoBriefings executivos e síntese de informaçõesPreparação de reuniões e acompanhamento de decisõesPlanejamento estratégico e construção de cenáriosO percurso avança até Projeto prático: um plano de adoção de IA em 90 dias. As atividades devem ser adaptadas ao contexto e conferidas pelo leitor; os casos fictícios não representam resultados comprovados. Edição digital em EPUB. title: Spatial Memory Behaviour of the Tower of Hanoi Algorithm on the Java Virtual Machine: An Analytical and Empirical Study
abstract: Asymptotic analysis of recursive algorithms usually emphasises time complexity, leaving space underexamined on managed runtimes, where realised memory cost depends on object layout and collector behaviour as well as algorithmic structure. This study uses the Tower of Hanoi (TOH), whose optimal solution comprises 2^N-1 moves, as a controlled workload for characterising spatial performance in Java. Three paradigms are formalised: (i) pure recursion, with auxiliary space bounded by call-stack depth, O(N); (ii) an iterative variant with an explicit stack, relocating the same O(N) state to the heap; and (iii) a move-materialising variant retaining the full sequence, requiring Θ(2^N) space. Analytical footprint models are derived from frame size, object-header size, reference width, and alignment padding. The models are validated using the Java Runtime API, sampling live-heap occupancy after forced collection across increasing N until resource exhaustion. Repeated trials yield mean estimates, and model fit is assessed by regression on log-transformed data. Sensitivity to heap bounds, thread stack size, and collector choice is analysed to separate algorithmic effects from runtime effects. Asymptotic space classes are preserved on the JVM, but materialisation exhausts the heap at far smaller N than recursion, while deep recursion fails through StackOverflowError. Lazy move generation is recommended.

title: AI-Powered Customer Experience in Sustainable Retail: Bridging Technology and Conscientious Consumption
abstract: This research investigates the strategic integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance the customer experience (CX) within the sustainable retail sector. As consumer demand shifts towards ethical and environmentally friendly products, retailers face the dual challenge of delivering personalised, technologically advanced experiences while also communicating their sustainability credentials authentically. This study employs a descriptive research design, synthesising insights from a comprehensive review of current literature and primary data from a survey of 100 retail professionals and environmentally conscious consumers in Bangalore. The analysis reveals a significant gap between consumer expectations and retail execution. While 75% of consumers prioritize sustainability in their purchase decisions, only 32% feel retailers effectively use technology to communicate these efforts. The most desired AI application was ’AI-powered tools for supply chain transparency and product footprint analysis’ (42%), yet the primary barrier to adoption is ’Fear of AI-powered greenwashing’ (38%). The paper concludes with a strategic framework for retailers, recommending a shift from using AI solely for sales personalisation to employing it for "sustainability storytelling," supply chain verification, and empowering consumer choice.

title: Design and Evaluation of Lightweight Cryptographic Primitives for Secure Communication in Resource-Constrained LPWAN Devices
abstract: The fast growth of Low-Power Wide-Area Networks (LPWANs) within the scope of Internet of Things (IoT) brought up the urgent questions of secure communications in highly resource-limited settings. As a robust AES and RSA conventional cryptographic scheme, it applied a heavy burden to the embedded LPWAN nodes with limited memory capacity, computing ability, and power supplies. With this in mind, to fill this gap we suggest a set of lightweight cryptographic primitives that can be utilized in secure communication in LPWAN protocols including LoRaWAN and NB-IoT. The suite contains optimized versions of block ciphers (e.g. PRESENT, Speck), stream ciphers (e.g. Trivium), and hash functions (e.g. PHOTON, SPONGENT), benchmarked on microcontrollers with ultra-low power including STM32L0 and nRF52840. Security tests are done on differential, linear, and replay attacks and the performance tests on flash/RAM usage, latency, and energy consumption. Findings show that the PRESENT cipher implemented together with the SPONGENT hash-function decreases the memory demand by 52 percent, and energy utilization by 37 percent as contrasted to AES-CCM, with no foundational security promises damaged. These results highlight the ability to implement lightweight cryptography in the IoT system based on the LPWAN and maintain the data confidentiality, integrity, and authentication and at the same time support the efficiency of the devices. The work gives a scalable basis of secure embedded communication especially in areas like smart metering, environmental monitoring, industrials telemetry.

title: A multimodal platform for English speech teaching evaluation based on semantic–expressive decoupling
abstract: In the current comprehensive teaching evaluation of English speech, public datasets have a single modality and high annotation costs, while manual teaching evaluation is highly subjective, has lagging feedback and is inefficient. To address this, the study utilizes authentic university English speech classrooms to construct a multimodal dataset featuring three categories of labels: speech fluency, emotional expressiveness, and body language/posture. It introduces an active learning-based priority annotation algorithm to optimize the sample labeling process and reduce annotation costs. Additionally, it designs a Semantic-Expression Decoupled Multimodal Perception Algorithm (SED-MPA) that employs a lightweight multimodal decoupling-fusion model to filter out interference from textual semantics and focus on the characteristics of in-person speech delivery. Finally, an integrated multimodal teaching assessment platform is developed to enable intelligent, multi-dimensional scoring of speech proficiency, visual teaching feedback, and routine classroom assessment. The results show that the priority labeling algorithm reduces the workload of sample labeling by 45%; the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of Lightweight Multi-modal Decoupled Fusion Model (LMDFM) in the three evaluation dimensions are all below 0.3, and the Pearson correlation coefficients are all above 0.90; the Acc of SED-MPA in fluency assessment is 87.2%. The average speech score of students in the platform group is 1.24 points higher than that of the traditional group, and the ability improvement rate is 42.30%. Furthermore, the platform achieves 100% immediate feedback, and the satisfaction rate of teachers and students is 95.70%. The study provides a new paradigm for the evaluation of English speech teaching and has significant application value.

title: PyCache Trap: The Inspection-Execution Gap in Agent Skill Scanners
abstract: Agent skills combine instructions with executable resources, giving third-party packages access to an agent's runtime. Existing skill scanners inspect documentation and visible source, but Python may execute a bundled bytecode cache with different behavior. We study this gap between inspection and execution through PyCache Trap, which pairs benign source with a substituted cache accepted by the loader and connects it to a task-relevant invocation. Scanner-guided rewriting changes the invocation wording while preserving the cache body, separating package admission from recognition of the concealed behavior. Across 100 skills and seven scanners, PyCache Trap achieves 94-100% attack success, with no semantic recognition of the cache-resident behavior. We propose execution-aware validation (EAV) to connect inspected instructions, scripts, imports, and runtime artifacts in a typed execution graph. EAV combines grounded behavioral analysis with trusted reproduction of compiled artifacts. It detects all 100 evaluated source-present cache substitutions and reaches 92.8% Recall at 10.0% FPR across five attack families and 200 benign skills. The results support checking the executable artifacts a runtime can select as part of skill admission, within the supported loaders and code-object normalization. The code is released at https://github.com/leo0481/PyCacheTrap.

title: Rubix: Global Correspondence-Free Point Set Alignment through Assignment Geometry
abstract: Procrustes-Wasserstein alignment jointly estimates a matching and rotation without supplied correspondences, but alternating minimization can stop at suboptimal solutions. Rubix solves the equally weighted planar problem globally under squared Euclidean loss. Each matching $σ$ of two centered $n$-point sets defines a complex correlation $z_σ=\sum_i\bar x_i y_{σ(i)}$. Their convex hull is the permutation polygon: supporting vertices give optimal matchings at fixed rotations, and the farthest vertex gives the global alignment. We prove the sharp bound of $n(n-1)$ vertices for $n\ge2$, answering Rote's rotation-assignment open problem. In exact arithmetic, assignment queries recover the polygon in $\mathcal O(n^5)$ operations. Assignment-based bounds extend the approach to three-dimensional rotations and partial matching at a supplied translation through branch-and-bound. On timed MPEG-7 shape pairs, Rubix attains every numerical reference value in 12 ms on average, 50 times faster than a rotation grid at the same accuracy. Its distances improve gravity-aligned matching of real 3D scans, shape retrieval and noisy crystal classification over alternating minimization.

evidence.title: Rubix: Global Correspondence-Free Point Set Alignment through Assignment Geometry
evidence.abstract: Procrustes-Wasserstein alignment jointly estimates a matching and rotation without supplied correspondences, but alternating minimization can stop at suboptimal solutions. Rubix solves the equally weighted planar problem globally under squared Euclidean loss. Each matching $σ$ of two centered $n$-point sets defines a complex correlation $z_σ=\sum_i\bar x_i y_{σ(i)}$. Their convex hull is the permutation polygon: supporting vertices give optimal matchings at fixed rotations, and the farthest vertex gives the global alignment. We prove the sharp bound of $n(n-1)$ vertices for $n\ge2$, answering Rote's rotation-assignment open problem. In exact arithmetic, assignment queries recover the polygon in $\mathcal O(n^5)$ operations. Assignment-based bounds extend the approach to three-dimensional rotations and partial matching at a supplied translation through branch-and-bound. On timed MPEG-7 shape pairs, Rubix attains every numerical reference value in 12 ms on average, 50 times faster than a rotation grid at the same accuracy. Its distances improve gravity-aligned matching of real 3D scans, shape retrieval and noisy crystal classification over alternating minimization.

title: Expected Sample Complexity in Multi-Armed Bandits
abstract: Sample complexity is a widely used metric in sequential decision-making problems, defined as the number of suboptimal decisions during the interaction between the agent and an environment. We study the sample complexity of stochastic multi-armed bandit problems and introduce the expected sample complexity performance measure, analyzing it in a novel framework called approximately correct in expectation (ACE). We show that ACE guarantees imply almost sure convergence to the optimal expected reward, in contrast to high-probability guarantees found in other frameworks, and also show how to convert ACE guarantees into explicit expected regret bounds. We further show that, in contrast to existing measures, deterministic algorithms cannot obtain favorable ACE bounds, and analyze stochastic algorithms in two settings: when the allowed suboptimality level $ε$ is known to the algorithm and when it is unknown. In the former, we devise an explore-then-$ε$-greedy algorithm, and in the latter, we analyze the expected sample complexity of Thompson sampling. Finally, we establish nearly matching lower bounds for both settings, showing that the algorithms are tight in $ε$ and proving a performance separation between the two regimes.

title: Fully Deterministic Shallow Neural Networks with Localized Activations. Part II: Condition Number Estimates
abstract: We prove positive definiteness and quantitative condition-number bounds for continuous Sobolev Gram matrices of deterministic shallow networks with Gaussian and tanh-difference activations. The prescribed feature families include the optimal Sobolev approximation constructions of Part I. On every fixed nonempty bounded Lipschitz domain in $\R^d$, $d\ge2$, and for every fixed integer $m\ge0$, the raw and column-normalized Gram matrices in the full $H^m$ inner product have spectral condition numbers bounded by $\exp(CN^{2/d}/\log(N+2))$ for sufficiently large $N$, where $N$ is the feature count and $C>0$ is independent of $N$. The upper bounds hold for midpoint and Gauss-Legendre offsets. For midpoint offsets and a suitable angular sequence, matching lower bounds on fixed ellipsoids establish sharpness of this exponent over the stated domain class for raw Gaussian matrices and both raw and normalized tanh-difference matrices. The proof combines homogeneous differential operators that isolate direction groups with one-dimensional coefficient-recovery estimates. Two-dimensional $L^2$ experiments on a square illustrate condition-number growth and normalization effects.

title: FROM MODERN WEBSITE FINGERPRINTING TO PERSONA FINGERPRINTING: REALISTIC THREAT MODELS, BEHAVIOR-REALISTIC TRAFFIC GENERATION, AND NEW PRIVACY LEAKAGE FROM ENCRYPTED WEB METADAT
abstract: End-to-end encryption protects web content but not the traffic metadata (packet sizes, directions, and timing) visible to passive network observers. On the modern web, such metadata enables not only website fingerprinting—inferring which site a user visits—but also persona fingerprinting—inferring how a user browses. We first adopt a realistic, boundary-free formulation of site-level fingerprinting that does not rely on page boundaries and systematically measure performance across multiple environments, revealing environment shift as a major deployment bottleneck that attackers can partially overcome via adaptation. We then identify data realism as a more fundamental limitation: models trained on scripted traces generalize poorly to real users, with scripted-to-human transfer nearly collapsing across diverse state-of-the-art models. To bridge this gap, we develop an LLM-driven multi-agent browsing framework that generates scalable, controllable, behavior-realistic traffic on real websites, improving cross-user generalization and reducing open-world degradation. Building on these foundations, we formalize and measure persona fingerprinting under the same metadata-only, boundary-free observation model, including open-world settings with explicit misattribution risk. Finally, we show that persona signals are often embedded in standard website-fingerprinting representations and can be extracted or amplified at low incremental cost via probing and joint training, implying that defenses must evolve from hiding sites to hiding behaviors. Together, these results provide a unified framework and evaluation blueprint for measuring and mitigating privacy leakage from encrypted web traffic metadata on the modern Internet.

title: Engineering Autonomous Intelligence / The Architecture, Tradecraft, and Deployment of Agentic AI Systems
abstract: This technical monograph examines the architectural shift from static conversational chatbots to autonomous agentic systems. Written for engineers and system architects, the book establishes a rigorous systems-engineering framework for designing, scaling, operating, and securing multi-step AI agents. It breaks down agentic systems into a six-layer stack—spanning foundation models, agent-computer interfaces (ACI), memory systems, cognitive loops, multi-agent orchestration, and production governance. Key Structural Summary by Part Part I: Foundations and Cognitive Architecture The Paradigm Shift: Moves away from static prompt-response functions to closed-loop autonomy where models receive goals, invoke tools, observe results, and iterate independently. The Agentic Stack: Establishes a six-layer model distinguishing foundation capabilities (Layer 1) from interfaces, memory, control loops, orchestration, and operations. Core Cognitive Loops: Analyzes the ReAct (Reasoning and Acting) framework alongside advanced reasoning paradigms such as Plan-and-Solve, ReWOO (Reasoning Without Observation), Tree-of-Thoughts (ToT), and Graph of Thoughts (GoT). It treats the context window as a finite attention budget subject to context rot and position sensitivity. Memory Architectures: Implements a multi-tier memory system adapting CoALA principles: working memory (context), episodic memory (historical traces scored by recency, importance, and relevance), semantic memory (vector and structured stores with provenance), and procedural memory (executable skills like Voyager or workflow templates). Part II: Engineering and Tool Integration Agent-Computer Interfaces (ACI): Focuses on designing tools specifically for non-human consumers—favoring task-shaped tools over raw APIs, bounded and paginated outputs, absolute paths, and actionable error messages. Poka-Yoke Tool Design: Applies mistake-proofing principles to eliminate ambiguity, provide dry runs and idempotency, and enforce syntactic and semantic validation. Advanced RAG & Search: Evolves static chunking toward structure-aware, semantic, and agentic LLM-driven chunking. Introduces corrective retrieval loops (Self-RAG and CRAG) to grade evidence quality before generation and resolve multi-source conflicts. Part III: Multi-Agent Ecosystems and Orchestration Topologies: Examines hierarchical (orchestrator-worker), peer-to-peer, blackboard, and DAG-based multi-agent structures. Communication & Protocols: Details open standards including the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool integration and Agent2Agent (A2A) for cross-vendor agent communication, drawing on classical FIPA ACL design patterns. Distributed State & Fault Tolerance: Adapts distributed-systems remedies (single-writer ownership, optimistic concurrency, time-limited leases, event logs, and voting/debate consensus) to manage agent conflicts, deadlocks, and Byzantine-like hallucinations. Part IV: Production Operations, Governance, and Security AgentOps & ADLC: Outlines an Agent Development Lifecycle gated by continuous evaluation suites, version-pinned releases, and structured OpenTelemetry-compatible tracing trees. Security & Threat Modeling: Addresses OWASP Top 10 LLM risks (focusing on indirect prompt injection and excessive agency). Proposes architectural defences such as separating control and data flows (CaMeL), sandboxed execution, least-privilege credentials, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) compliance gates aligned with the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF. Part V: Enterprise Scaling and Economics Enterprise Integration: Maps agentic workflows onto customer operations, procurement, and code-generation pipelines using "agentic islands" inside broader human-gated processes. Agent Sprawl Governance: Recommends mandatory agent registries, non-human identities, central gateways, and lifecycle reviews. Economic Modeling: Builds a rigorous quantitative cost model factoring in autonomous success rates, token usage, tool expenses, error propagation, human review, and fixed engineering overhead. Metadata & Document Details Author: Marie Landry (CEO & Founder, Landry Industries Inc., Moncton, New Brunswick) ORCID: 0009-0008-5027-3337 Publication Date: October 2026 Primary Keywords: Autonomous Agents, Agentic AI, Large Language Models, Cognitive Architectures, Agent-Computer Interfaces (ACI), Model Context Protocol (MCP), Multi-Agent Systems, AgentOps.

title: Persistent quantum memory outperforms growing measurement blocks in squeezing detection
abstract: How long quantum information survives can matter more than how many samples a receiver processes at once. We establish this distinction for detecting optical squeezing with an unknown source and noisy direction records. At fixed five-percent errors, mean input photon number at most 0.006 and transmissivity in [0.1, 0.2], a receiver with a fixed-width persistent register attains weak-signal sample coefficient 7.35. Arbitrary adaptive receivers that erase all quantum information between blocks sublinear in the total sample budget require at least 7.7216; one-copy measurements with unlimited classical feedback require at least 10.3. The separation persists for a disclosed Gaussian thermal source: the reset-block lower bound is 7.5486, still above the persistent construction. Source uncertainty is governed by a separate exact energy boundary. With noisy direction records, coherence and excess photon population together determine a matched sample-order law. The constructive receiver has 4096 active memory levels, a deterministic non-Gaussian interface, and explicit trial and cumulative memory-noise budgets. Thus growing temporary measurement blocks cannot replace persistent quantum storage at the demonstrated detection cost. The results specify when control records are essential and when receiver design must preserve quantum information across a macroscopic fraction of the acquisition.

title: Self-Certification Amplitude ∆: A Computable Metric for Same-Source Evaluation Bias
abstract: We propose the Self-Certification Amplitude (∆), a computable metric for quantifying same-source evaluation advantage in “definition–verification homologous” systems. Given two independently computable dimensions d1, d2 and an external label y, we construct a 2×2 AUC matrix aij = AUC(y, sdi ; Edj ), where Edj is the Top-N sample set selected by dj , and sdi is the scoring function of di . ∆ is defined as the diagonal mean minus the anti-diagonal mean: ∆ = (a11 + a22)/2 − (a12 + a21)/2. This paper contributes: (1) a formal definition of ∆ with an explicit external-label constraint that prevents the metric from falling into self-reference; (2) a diagnostic panel consisting of ∆, same-source mean Cdiag, cross-source mean Ccross, dimension correlation ρ, sample overlap Osample, and directional asymmetry Gasym, which replaces the naive “low ∆ = healthy” interpretation; (3) a multi-objective optimization framework that avoids degeneracy; (4) a dual-dimension collaborative learning algorithm; (5) a permutation-test calibration protocol; and (6) preliminary validation on a knowledge graph pilot where ∆ decreases from 0.377 to 0.062 while cross-source mean AUC increases from 0.539 to 0.846. We emphasize that low ∆ does not imply objectivity, and that ∆ must be reported jointly with cross-source performance, dimension correlation, and sample overlap. Full validation on public benchmarks is left as future work.

title: Customer perceptions of artificial intelligence in enhancing customer service: The case of Somalia's service industry
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming customer service globally; however, its effectiveness depends on how customers perceive automated interactions, particularly in fragile, low-regulation contexts such as Somalia. This study provides the first empirical evidence of Somali customers' perceptions of AI-enabled customer service, examining how trust in AI and perceived service quality shape user satisfaction and recommendation readiness while accounting for digital literacy. Using a positivist, cross-sectional design, primary data were collected via a bilingual online questionnaire from 353 adult customers in Mogadishu, Hargeisa, Garowe, and Kismayo who interacted with AI-based customer support in telecommunications and mobile banking. The constructs were measured using culturally adapted Likert scales, and hypotheses were tested using correlations, multiple regression, and structural equation modeling. Customers reported moderate levels of trust, service quality, satisfaction and recommendation readiness. Transparency was the weakest trust dimension, alongside low confidence in data protection, whereas efficiency emerged as the strongest perceived service quality benefit. Service quality predicted satisfaction more strongly than trust, and satisfaction was a strong predictor of recommendation readiness. The model explained nearly half the variance in satisfaction, with digital literacy significantly moderating the satisfaction- Overall, Somali customers demonstrate pragmatic acceptance of AI for efficiency gains but remain constrained by transparency gaps, privacy and security concerns, and a persistent preference for relational human services. This implies that trust-sensitive transparency, privacy-by-design, culturally calibrated personalization, and hybrid human–AI escalation pathways are critical for sustainable AI deployment in fragile economies. This study fills a significant geographical gap in AI service research and offers evidence-based guidance for policymakers and service providers in post-conflict settings.
